I'm not super loud, but it's still enough to bother him. He's upset, and I can see why he would be. On the other hand, my friends are also playing late, and I'm just joining them. I'm not the only one causing noise, but I'm contributing to it. I want to continue playing because it's something I enjoy, but I also need to consider my roommate's need for a quiet environment to sleep. Is it morally acceptable to continue playing late if I try to keep it quiet? Well, morally, I think it's about balancing my own interests with the well-being of my roommate. I should also consider the fairness aspect. If my friends are playing late and not early, why should I be the one to stop? But the difference is that I'm directly affecting my roommate's ability to sleep, whereas my friends might not be in the same living situation as me. Maybe I should talk to my roommate and find a compromise. Perhaps we can set some quiet hours or find a time when I can play without disturbing him. That way, both of our needs are met. It's important to respect each other's needs and find a solution that works for everyone.
